requirements.quote:
Many transport parameters listed here have integer values.  Those
   transport parameters that are identified as integers use a variable-
   length integer encoding; see Section 16.  Transport parameters have a
   default value of 0 if the transport parameter is absent, unless
   otherwise stated.
requirements.condition: A transport parameter is identified as an integer.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the parameter using variable-length integer encoding.
requirements.why_checkable: The wire encoding used for every integer-valued transport parameter can be inspected.

requirements.quote:

requirements.condition: A transport parameter is absent and no parameter-specific default is stated.
requirements.required_behavior: Use 0 as the parameter value.
requirements.why_checkable: Parameter parsing and initialization can be tested for an omitted parameter without an overriding default.

requirements.quote:
original_destination_connection_id (0x00):  This parameter is the
      value of the Destination Connection ID field from the first
      Initial packet sent by the client; see Section 7.3.  This
      transport parameter is only sent by a server.
requirements.condition: The original_destination_connection_id transport parameter is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Use transport parameter identifier 0x00.
requirements.why_checkable: The parameter type identifier is directly observable in the encoded transport parameters.

requirements.quote:

requirements.condition: A server sends original_destination_connection_id.
requirements.required_behavior: Set its value to the Destination Connection ID field from the first Initial packet sent by the client.
requirements.why_checkable: A captured first client Initial can be compared byte-for-byte with the server's parameter value.

requirements.quote:
max_idle_timeout (0x01):  The maximum idle timeout is a value in
      milliseconds that is encoded as an integer; see (Section 10.1).
      Idle timeout is disabled when both endpoints omit this transport
      parameter or specify a value of 0.
requirements.condition: The max_idle_timeout transport parameter is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Use transport parameter identifier 0x01 and represent its value in milliseconds as an integer.
requirements.why_checkable: The identifier and integer value on the wire can be inspected and interpreted in the specified unit.

requirements.quote:
max_idle_timeout (0x01):  The maximum idle timeout is a value in
      milliseconds that is encoded as an integer; see (Section 10.1).
      Idle timeout is disabled when both endpoints omit this transport
      parameter or specify a value of 0.
requirements.condition: Both endpoints omit max_idle_timeout or specify max_idle_timeout as 0.
requirements.required_behavior: Disable idle timeout.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Terminate the connection because an idle timeout elapsed.
requirements.why_checkable: A connection can be left idle under the stated negotiation and observed for timeout-based termination.

requirements.quote:
stateless_reset_token (0x02):  A stateless reset token is used in
      verifying a stateless reset; see Section 10.3.  This parameter is
      a sequence of 16 bytes.  This transport parameter MUST NOT be sent
      by a client but MAY be sent by a server.  A server that does not
      send this transport parameter cannot use stateless reset
      (Section 10.3) for the connection ID negotiated during the
      handshake.
requirements.condition: The stateless_reset_token transport parameter is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Use transport parameter identifier 0x02 and a value exactly 16 bytes long.
requirements.why_checkable: The parameter identifier and value length are directly observable on the wire.

requirements.quote:
max_udp_payload_size (0x03):  The maximum UDP payload size parameter
      is an integer value that limits the size of UDP payloads that the
      endpoint is willing to receive.  UDP datagrams with payloads
      larger than this limit are not likely to be processed by the
      receiver.
requirements.condition: The max_udp_payload_size transport parameter is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Use transport parameter identifier 0x03 and encode its value as an integer.
requirements.why_checkable: The parameter identifier and integer representation are directly inspectable.

requirements.quote:
max_udp_payload_size (0x03):  The maximum UDP payload size parameter
      is an integer value that limits the size of UDP payloads that the
      endpoint is willing to receive.  UDP datagrams with payloads
      larger than this limit are not likely to be processed by the
      receiver.
requirements.condition: An endpoint advertises max_udp_payload_size.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the value as the limit on UDP payload sizes the endpoint is willing to receive.
requirements.why_checkable: Receiver behavior and accepted payload sizes can be tested against the advertised integer limit.

requirements.quote:
The default for this parameter is the maximum permitted UDP
      payload of 65527.  Values below 1200 are invalid.
requirements.condition: max_udp_payload_size is absent.
requirements.required_behavior: Use 65527 as its value.
requirements.why_checkable: The effective receive limit can be checked when the parameter is omitted.

requirements.quote:
The default for this parameter is the maximum permitted UDP

requirements.condition: A max_udp_payload_size value is received or configured.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Accept a value below 1200 as valid.
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary values below and at 1200 can be supplied to the transport-parameter parser.

requirements.quote:
initial_max_data (0x04):  The initial maximum data parameter is an
      integer value that contains the initial value for the maximum
      amount of data that can be sent on the connection.  This is
      equivalent to sending a MAX_DATA (Section 19.9) for the connection
      immediately after completing the handshake.
requirements.condition: The initial_max_data transport parameter is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Use transport parameter identifier 0x04 and encode its value as an integer.
requirements.why_checkable: The identifier and integer encoding are visible in the transport parameters.

requirements.quote:
initial_max_data (0x04):  The initial maximum data parameter is an
      integer value that contains the initial value for the maximum
      amount of data that can be sent on the connection.  This is
      equivalent to sending a MAX_DATA (Section 19.9) for the connection
      immediately after completing the handshake.
requirements.condition: initial_max_data is received.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply its value as the initial maximum amount of data that can be sent on the connection, equivalent to a MAX_DATA with that value immediately after handshake completion.
requirements.why_checkable: The sender's permitted connection-level data can be tested immediately after the handshake against the parameter value.

requirements.quote:
initial_max_stream_data_bidi_local (0x05):  This parameter is an
      integer value specifying the initial flow control limit for
      locally initiated bidirectional streams.  This limit applies to
      newly created bidirectional streams opened by the endpoint that
      sends the transport parameter.  In client transport parameters,
      this applies to streams with an identifier with the least
      significant two bits set to 0x00; in server transport parameters,
      this applies to streams with the least significant two bits set to
      0x01.
requirements.condition: The initial_max_stream_data_bidi_local transport parameter is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Use transport parameter identifier 0x05 and encode its value as an integer.
requirements.why_checkable: The identifier and integer encoding are directly observable.

requirements.quote:
initial_max_stream_data_bidi_local (0x05):  This parameter is an
      integer value specifying the initial flow control limit for
      locally initiated bidirectional streams.  This limit applies to
      newly created bidirectional streams opened by the endpoint that
      sends the transport parameter.  In client transport parameters,

requirements.condition: A client sends initial_max_stream_data_bidi_local.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply the value as the initial flow-control limit for newly created bidirectional streams whose identifiers have least significant two bits 0x00 and that are opened by the client.
requirements.why_checkable: Stream identifiers and initial per-stream send limits can be tested after negotiation.

requirements.quote:
initial_max_streams_bidi (0x08):  The initial maximum bidirectional
      streams parameter is an integer value that contains the initial
      maximum number of bidirectional streams the endpoint that receives
      this transport parameter is permitted to initiate.  If this
      parameter is absent or zero, the peer cannot open bidirectional
      streams until a MAX_STREAMS frame is sent.  Setting this parameter
      is equivalent to sending a MAX_STREAMS (Section 19.11) of the
      corresponding type with the same value.
requirements.condition: The initial_max_streams_bidi transport parameter is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Use transport parameter identifier 0x08 and encode its value as an integer.
requirements.why_checkable: The identifier and integer encoding are directly observable.

requirements.quote:
initial_max_streams_bidi (0x08):  The initial maximum bidirectional
      streams parameter is an integer value that contains the initial
      maximum number of bidirectional streams the endpoint that receives
      this transport parameter is permitted to initiate.  If this
      parameter is absent or zero, the peer cannot open bidirectional
      streams until a MAX_STREAMS frame is sent.  Setting this parameter
      is equivalent to sending a MAX_STREAMS (Section 19.11) of the
      corresponding type with the same value.
requirements.condition: initial_max_streams_bidi is present with a nonzero value.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the receiving endpoint to initiate at most that initial number of bidirectional streams, equivalently to a corresponding-type MAX_STREAMS frame with the same value.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Permit the receiving endpoint to initiate more bidirectional streams than the value allows before a later limit increase.
requirements.why_checkable: The number of bidirectional streams accepted before a later MAX_STREAMS limit increase can be counted.

requirements.quote:
initial_max_streams_bidi (0x08):  The initial maximum bidirectional

requirements.condition: initial_max_streams_bidi is absent or zero and no subsequent MAX_STREAMS frame has been sent.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Allow the peer to open a bidirectional stream.
requirements.why_checkable: A peer can attempt to open a bidirectional stream before any MAX_STREAMS frame and the implementation response can be observed.

requirements.quote:
ack_delay_exponent (0x0a):  The acknowledgment delay exponent is an
      integer value indicating an exponent used to decode the ACK Delay
      field in the ACK frame (Section 19.3).  If this value is absent, a
      default value of 3 is assumed (indicating a multiplier of 8).
      Values above 20 are invalid.
requirements.condition: The ack_delay_exponent transport parameter is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Use transport parameter identifier 0x0a and encode its value as an integer.
requirements.why_checkable: The identifier and integer encoding are directly observable.

requirements.quote:
ack_delay_exponent (0x0a):  The acknowledgment delay exponent is an
      integer value indicating an exponent used to decode the ACK Delay
      field in the ACK frame (Section 19.3).  If this value is absent, a
      default value of 3 is assumed (indicating a multiplier of 8).
      Values above 20 are invalid.
requirements.condition: An ack_delay_exponent value is available.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the value as the exponent when decoding the ACK Delay field in ACK frames.
requirements.why_checkable: ACK Delay decoding results can be compared with the advertised exponent.

requirements.quote:
ack_delay_exponent (0x0a):  The acknowledgment delay exponent is an

requirements.condition: ack_delay_exponent is absent.
requirements.required_behavior: Assume an exponent of 3, corresponding to a multiplier of 8.
requirements.why_checkable: ACK Delay decoding with an omitted parameter can be checked against exponent 3.
